solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awesome shape I would fit

blocks.note: form is another word for shape
I'd is the contraction of I would
fit to do something means able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a figure that fits perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formidable inspires awe or fear, so awesome is a close synonym.

clue.text: Old sour smell

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a dour person is sour and gloomy

explanation.surface: A stale, sour whiff from something past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, usually a noticeable or unpleasant one, so the two are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe put wrong year on new Times ad

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters that follow are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh advert in The Times newspaper carries the wrong year by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The setting's own newspaper supplies the letters; 'Maybe' signals that a wrong year is only one way of giving a wrong date.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdate is to give something an incorrect date, and a wrong year is one example of that error.

clue.text: Study conclusions of Edward Theodore Compton

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the final letter of each following name is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of each of the three names

explanation.surface: Someone researching the findings of a scholar called Edward Theodore Compton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb about research, but it is the noun for a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room for work or retreat, which is also what a study is.

clue.text: Excellent train bill rewritten

indicators.note: text that is rewritten comes out in a different form, so these letters are set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a rail bill that has been redrafted for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant is an everyday synonym for outstanding or superb.

clue.text: Scottish town's extremely ethical spirit

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are used

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
gin is a spirit, a strong distilled drink

explanation.surface: A Scottish town is said to have a highly moral character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' seems to mean the town's moral character but is the drink. Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is an example of a Scottish town, the historic centre of Moray.

clue.text: Hope tears up in A&E

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards
in tells us one piece sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: the letters A and E, the hospital emergency department's abbreviation
rips as a verb, tears apart

explanation.surface: Someone in hospital emergency, hoping, while tearing up with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears up' suggests weeping; here tears means rips, read upwards. A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or long to achieve something, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Arsenic, say, is put in spoon when leader's away

indicators.note: with its leader gone, a word loses its first letter
put in tells us one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisoner slips arsenic into a spoon while the boss is out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the S of spoon leaves POON, which then takes IS in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a classic example of a poison, hence the 'say' marking it as one instance.

clue.text: Take in part of housing estate

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a stretch of letters lying inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone taking in a section of a residential estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, swallowing it.

clue.text: American dream exposed subject of interest

indicators.note: something exposed has its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go and the inside remains

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: The American Dream laid bare as something worth studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American dream' reads as one famous phrase, but the two words are worked separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An area can mean a field of study or particular topic, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Fine to fork out, holding learner driving licence, perhaps

indicators.note: holding means grasping something within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to fork out is to spend money
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a driving licence is one example of identification

explanation.surface: A penalty to pay while carrying a provisional licence for driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty, which fits 'fork out', but it means excellent. Learner drivers in Britain display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means excellent or very good, as does fine in 'a fine performance'.

clue.text: Sick person might need this rest, unfortunately broken by vomit

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately goes wrong, so the word's letters end up out of order
to be broken by something is to have it inserted, splitting the outer letters

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
to retch is to heave as if to vomit

explanation.surface: An ill patient's rest is spoilt by bouts of being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick person' suggests the vomit belongs in the definition, but the whole first phrase defines and 'vomit' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a frame for carrying an ill or injured person, which such a patient might need.

clue.text: Quickly move profession

blocks.note: first meaning: to rush along fast and out of control
second meaning: a person's working life or occupation

explanation.surface: Advice to change jobs fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for hurtling at speed and a noun for one's chosen line of work.

clue.text: US state also known as being host for Vegas opener?

indicators.note: an opener comes at the start, so we keep the opening word of the famous city's name
a host has a guest within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: aka is the usual abbreviation of the phrase
the first word of the full city name Las Vegas

explanation.surface: A US state described as hosting the opening of a Las Vegas show.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stretch: the opener of Vegas is the word that comes before it in Las Vegas, not its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is one of the fifty United States, the largest by area.

clue.text: Demonstrator ignoring first shooter?

indicators.note: ignoring the first means leaving off the word's opening letter

blocks.note: a marcher takes part in a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A protester who disregards the leading marcher.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows with a bow, so is one kind of shooter, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Perhaps Ottawa is excellent

blocks.note: first meaning: a seat of government, Ottawa being Canada's
second meaning: first-rate, an old-fashioned exclamation of approval

explanation.surface: A claim that Canada's chief city is a fine place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a country's seat of government and is also a dated adjective for first-rate.

clue.text: Strenuously working trait had to change

indicators.note: a change of form means these letters are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy person whose character trait needed altering.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hard at it is an idiom for being busily and energetically engaged in work.

clue.text: Piece of information at university within direct message

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so these pieces sit in the middle of another

blocks.note: DM is the social-media abbreviation for a direct message
taken as written
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A fact about college life sent over private message.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of data, the singular of data.

clue.text: Alliance's power play

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A coalition's political manoeuvre for power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power play' reads as one phrase about political manoeuvring but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement binding parties together, as an alliance does.

clue.text: Mate could complete this part of French essay

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a run of letters within the following words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A friend could finish off a section of a homework essay in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a friend helping with homework; it is checkmate, which ends the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate ends a game of this board game, so mate completes it.

clue.text: Outline of small ship

blocks.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: The silhouette or plan of a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief outline of the main features of something.

clue.text: Servant in trouble, worried with nothing set aside

indicators.note: nothing is a zero, the round letter, and setting it aside removes it
something worried is troubled and unsettled, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing a letter
O looks like a zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A household servant in a fix, anxious and left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the O from the word leaves TRUBLE, whose letters then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household, so is a type of servant.

clue.text: Life belt is optional at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A safety warning that life-saving belts were once not compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life belt' reads as a lifebelt, but 'Life' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bio is a short biography, an account of someone's life.

clue.text: Some sorrel scattered around

indicators.note: things scattered are spread about in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener describing a herb strewn over the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a quantity word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: More or less means approximately, as does around before a number.
